title: Buddy Petit's shifting band and its drummers
summary: Petit used changing sidemen; Jiles names clarinetists, trombonists, drummers, bassists and sax, and prefers clarinet to sax.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: You talked about him, who did he have with him?

Well he would use Zeb, Melvin, different ones too, because he was a fellow who had two and three jobs at the same time. At that time some of the band was not exactly standard, but the band went by the leader who, he used his name as Buddy Petit Band, but we'd come tonight maybe with Melvin. Next time he'd come with Zeb, Georgie Boyle, you know.
So he'd change up all the time. Yeah. Well who else would he have with him say on trombone? Do you remember any particular guy who stands out in your mind?
Yeah, he used Harrison Bradley, Harrison Bones, Ambrose.
What about in the rhythm? Who would he have?
Peter Pappy, and he had some time, and Guy Yeh, you know talk of him. Used to play a jitney man for him. He got killed. Walter.
You played drums with him sometimes?

With Buddy Petit? Yeah I played jobs too. Never played regular, but I mean occasionally like I said they'd get two jobs. Be lucky enough to get in. You see at that time if a fellow played with one of them guys, the other guy would be looking for you to prove satisfaction you know. And then.
Who was Buddy's drummer regular? Did he have anybody regular on drums?
Well at certain times Faye so played with him a good while. Alfred, he used Benny, which I never know if Benny is right then, you heard talk of him.
Which Benny was this?
Black Benny they called him, you heard talk of him. Yeah. Guys like him.
And which Alfred is that?
The one I know? Yeah. We called him Levin and Alfred.
Levin?
We called him that. We called him that. But yeah that's the album.
He lives back what is it, around Conti Street and he plays with the Tuxedo now. That one Alfred used to be with Sam Moore in years and years. That's right.
That's right.
Alfred Williams.
Yeah.
That's a funny.
Let's see.
Do you have any piano players with anybody much?

Well occasionally certain jobs that he had piano players. He had a woman, I don't know her name, May, well he still had her playing with him. He had a job, but he wasn't, I mean regular, piano players.
And bass, I guess that's who we got left.
You mean playing with Buddy? Mm-hmm. He used the old man Albert Glennon, Johnny Predorch, you heard talk of that dude man, he was good too. He used the old time, he was good too.
Would he ever use the saxophone Buddy?
Oh at times, yeah. He used the saxophone, used Israel Garman playing saxophone. You see, at that time Israel used to use the saxophone in clarinets.
Was saxophone going over big then or what did it do?

Well it was something strange to the people. They thought it was good. But I always figured a clarinet for Dixieland's band was the best. You see a saxophone is more data-like, a clarinet is more sharper. It fits in better for Dixieland's band.
